candidates.why: Line 837 frees each did->counta[i]; line 841 then frees the containing array did->counta. If LEPT_FREE is a macro that reads the pointer (e.g. to null it or log it), the array is still valid here, but the element pointers freed at 837 are not cleared, so any later traversal of did->counta would be a use-after-free. Suspicious.

Line 838 frees each did->delya[i]; line 842 frees the containing array did->delya. The freed element pointers are not nulled, so any subsequent access through did->delya would be a use-after-free. Suspicious.

Line 862 frees did; line 863 writes recog->did = NULL. This is only an assignment, not a read of the freed block, so it is not a use-after-free. No genuine post-free dereference of did appears in lines 862-864.
